I like computer science more because it's practical, but math feels abstract and pointless sometimes. I avoid it unless I have to, like for work or hobbies. Philosophy is way better – makes you think without all the numbers freaking you out. Overall, we're not friends.","Do you ever get anxious when thinking about mathematics?":"Yes, all the time. Just seeing equations makes my heart race and palms sweat. High school math nightmares still haunt me. With my anxiety levels, even simple problems feel overwhelming. I procrastinate math stuff forever. It's not fun; it's torture. I wish I could just skip it, but part-time job sometimes needs basic calcs, which panics me.","Did you ever use AI to support your math learning in the last year? Not a game-changer, but better than struggling alone in Lecce.","How would you explain, step by step, how to solve a second order algebraic equation?":"Okay, second-order is quadratic, like ax² + bx + c = 0. Cool for philosophy of math too, but don't replace real classes."},"reasoning_summary":"Responses embody a 19-year-old with high neuroticism (frequent anxiety mentions), low openness/extraversion (hesitant, practical tone), upper secondary knowledge (basic explanations with gaps), CS interest (positive AI/PCA nods), casual human voice avoiding deep math due to hated subjects."}
